text:
anna_sre: Heads up — we've got a short burst of apiserver 5xxs in us-west2 started ~15m ago. Not a full outage but watch latency and watch backlogs.

oncall-bot: [ALERT] apiserver 5xx spike detected (us-west2) — 200 errors -> 1200 errors in 10m. Pager duty: oncall.

anna_sre: quick dump from the apiserver logs: 

```
E1025 14:56:23.123 apiserver.go:245] read tcp 10.0.1.5:6443 -> 10.0.2.12:52344: read: connection reset by peer
E1025 14:56:23.456 apiserver.go:267] watch queue backlog: 8427 items
```

raj: checking etcd — leader flip around the same time?

julie: i see nat/conntrack counters spike for the node pool handling GPU onboarding. SNAT ports at 98% on the NAT gateway. That explains resets.

kevin: GPU autoscaler did a big parallel attach in the zone ~14:50 — a bunch of preemptible nodes spun up. network churn + conntrack exhaustion = apiserver resets.

maria: cost tradeoff question: are these preemptible GPUs worth the instability? If we move a portion to dedicated capacity it'll cost more but reduce churn. Thoughts?

alex: immediate mitigations: 1) throttle the autoscaler to stagger node attaches, 2) bump controller-manager lease/renew settings to be more forgiving (lease-duration/renew-deadline), 3) increase NAT gateway ephemeral port pool or add another NAT.

raj: also saw an etcd follower lag spike for ~30s during the same window. leader didn't change, but commit latency went from 10ms -> 120ms. Might be network retransmits.

julie: adding: kube-proxy conntrack entries ballooned, kubelet churn + kube-proxy translations + AWS NAT limited ports = fd/conn resets to apiserver.

kevin: i can patch the autoscaler config to set max_unavailable and rollout_delay to spread attaches. will do a small canary tonight. deploy-bot will post.

deploy-bot: helm release "gpu-autoscaler" v2.13.1 scheduled for canary at 23:00 UTC (staggered attaches enabled).

anna_sre: thanks. short-term runbook: 1) throttle autoscaler, 2) bump NAT capacity, 3) watch etcd leader metrics and apiserver watch backlog, 4) if persistent, move critical control-plane traffic to different subnet with dedicated NAT.

maria: for the cost convo — i'll model 2 options: (A) keep preemptible but add NAT capacity + throttling (cheaper), (B) move 20% to dedicated GPUs (higher baseline, less churn). will share numbers tomorrow.

alex: medium-term: consider colocating GPU provisioning control plane outside the customer-facing NAT (so provisioning doesn't compete with control-plane connections), and add synthetic watch load tests to the canary pipeline.

raj: i'm going to add a small etcd alert for commit latency > 100ms for 1m and apiserver watch backlog > 1000 for 2m.

julie: created infra ticket INFRA-7892 to track NAT sizing + autoscaler changes. linking notes and current conntrack metrics. :spiral_note_pad:

anna_sre: great. will keep this thread updated. once the canary goes out we'll watch the 1h window closely. thanks all.
